PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use harness-owned plugin enablement in customizations
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #347318 for #347317.

## Summary

- Make Copilot-owned plugin activation authoritative in the harness, not workbench or Agent Host enablement overlays.
- Publish disabled and contentless installed plugins, with global state and exact-chat effective state kept separate.
- Route customization controls through runtime-owned global/repository mutations; remove session-only activation and local workspace overrides for these plugins.
- Gate controls on host support, organizational management, plugin source, and chat readiness; expose unavailable reasons visually and accessibly.
- Show an inline enablement switch, disabled with an explanation until the selected chat is ready. Use "Waiting for Session Start" for pending activation; omit redundant Loaded/Disabled badges when a switch is present.
- Avoid forwarding native plugins as additional plugins or manufacturing MCP changes from parent activation. Preserve explicit MCP child decisions, workspace deduplication, and other-provider behavior.
- Retain native agent picker metadata, route MCP child enablement through its owning plugin, preserve advertised default-chat activation on read-only hosts, and resolve duplicate contributions using runtime activation.
- Isolate inventory failures, recover discovery with bounded retries, and cache parsed native plugin content with file/version/installation invalidation.

Repository persistence continues to use the isolated settings writer introduced in #347318 until scoped SDK mutation is available. This does not migrate standalone MCP enablement ownership.

The initial publication additionally passed a full product build, the related Node suites, and layer checks. These were not repeated for this update. No E2E tests or recorded fixtures were changed.

### Live validation

Readiness and persistence were exercised in an isolated signed-in Code OSS window on macOS:

1. Verify the pending plugin switch and global action are disabled, with an accessible readiness explanation.
2. Complete a harmless real request and verify plugin enablement becomes available.
3. Enable the fixture plugin with the switch and independently verify harness-managed persistence.
4. Disable it with the keyboard and verify persisted state returns to its original value.
5. Reload and verify the exact "Waiting for Session Start" label and disabled switch before session readiness.

This live validation preceded the final inventory/discovery review fixes; those have the automated coverage above. Repository activation and remote hosts were not exercised live. The fixture was a direct installation, whose repository action remains disabled. No existing user plugin state was mutated.

## Manual testing

With a Copilot chat, open Chat Customizations → Plugins. Before session readiness, verify the disabled enablement switch and "Waiting for Session Start" label. Start the session, verify the switch becomes available, and check global persistence. For a marketplace-installed plugin, verify repository actions and reopen the chat to confirm effective state. Direct installations must keep repository actions disabled, and no session-only action should appear. Also check that organization-managed plugins and hosts without plugin-management support remain read-only.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The queue semantics, callers, and downstream RPCs are explicit; only the runtime-specific RPC duration varies.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every caller enqueues a distinct refresh; each executes one global SDK RPC and optionally a second live-session RPC, so work grows with snapshot, publication, and file-change frequency across active sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked create/resume paths and queued IPC latency during bursts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, session customization snapshots did not refresh the runtime plugin inventory and therefore did not queue these SDK RPCs.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new refresh method uses Sequencer.queue for every request. Settled and applied customization snapshots now call it unconditionally, while the queued operation reaches listPluginInstallations(session), which performs global plugins.list and then live-session plugins.list when available.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 12046 introduces per-request sequencing for runtime inventory refreshes; unlike coalescing, Sequencer executes every queued task.
Findings.Title: Coalesce queued runtime inventory refreshes
Findings.Impact: Concurrent session startup, customization publication, or watcher notifications serialize repeated inventory round trips even when all callers need the same unchanged result.
Findings.Evidence: The added line 12046 queues _readRuntimePlugins without retaining or reusing an in-flight/current promise. Added calls from getCustomizationsSettled and getAppliedCustomizations put it on create/resume and publication critical paths. The installedPlugins callback is wired to listPluginInstallations(session), whose implementation performs the SDK RPCs serially.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep one current/in-flight inventory promise per session and have concurrent readers share it. Invalidate and start a new refresh only after plugin mutations, runtime plugin-change events, or explicit discovery invalidation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The ownership, first-use call path, parser filesystem operations, and session lifetime are explicit in code. The exact OS watcher deduplication is implementation-dependent, but duplicate parse work, cache objects, file-change listeners, and per-session publications remain certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem reads plus recursive watcher and file-change listener objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With S active Copilot configuration scopes and P installed plugins, cold parsing and retained watch/listener state grow as S×P; changing one plugin also wakes each session-local listener and causes each session to reparse and republish independently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: duplicated filesystem I/O and CPU during session creation/resume, increased retained watcher/listener memory, and update-time I/O bursts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, SessionPluginController did not discover, parse, cache, or recursively watch every runtime-owned installed plugin; those per-session S×P resources and reads were absent from this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each SessionPluginController now owns its own ResourceMap of parsed plugin promises and DisposableResourceMap of watchers. Its first runtime inventory refresh maps every installation through _readRuntimePluginContents, which creates a recursive watch/listener and invokes parsePlugin for that session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 11886 adds the parsed-content cache directly to each newly created SessionPluginController (with the watcher map on the next added line), making cache and watch ownership per session rather than shared by installed plugin resource.
Findings.Title: Share runtime plugin parsing across sessions
Findings.Impact: Users with several installed plugins and multiple live Copilot sessions repeatedly pay the same manifest/component directory reads when sessions start or resume, retain duplicate listeners for the lifetime of those sessions, and fan a plugin update out across every session.
Findings.Evidence: The added session-local fields at lines 11886-11887 are consumed by _readRuntimePlugins, which Promise.all-parses every installed resource. _readRuntimePluginContents registers fileService.watch(resource, { recursive: true }) and a global onDidFilesChange listener, then calls PluginController.tryParsePlugin. parsePlugin detects format, reads the manifest, resolves component directories, and reads agent/skill/instruction files. Active clients are keyed per configuration scope and these resources live until _finalizeConfigurationScope disposes that session.
Findings.Recommendation: Move parsed runtime plugin content and its recursive invalidation watcher to PluginController (or another provider-wide, ref-counted cache) keyed by resource/version. Let sessions share the parsed promise and subscribe to one invalidation signal while keeping only chat-specific activation in SessionPluginController.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The blocking await and complete IPC/RPC path are explicit. Actual latency varies between local and remote hosts, so severity is low despite high mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host IPC/network calls and downstream Copilot SDK plugins.list RPCs
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each uncached item-provider fetch issues one inventory call per distinct runtime provider (providers run in parallel); for Copilot each call expands to one global SDK RPC and optionally one session RPC. The work repeats whenever the item source is recreated or invalidated, independent of plugin count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: longer time to render the customization management list, especially for remote agent hosts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The provider previously projected the already-published customization snapshot immediately and began plugin expansion without any management-service or runtime SDK inventory round trip.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The provider now awaits resolveRuntimePluginEnablement before iterating any customizations. That resolver has no cache and calls target.listPluginInstallations for every represented provider; the Copilot implementation performs global and optional session plugins.list RPCs serially.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 363 moves runtime inventory resolution onto provideChatSessionCustomizations' blocking path; before the hunk the method used getCustomizations(sessionResource) directly.
Findings.Title: Avoid blocking customization enumeration on fresh inventory RPCs
Findings.Impact: Opening or refreshing Chat Customizations cannot show any host items until the remote/runtime inventory completes, adding visible panel latency even though most item metadata is already in the session snapshot.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 363 awaits resolution before the item-building loop. AbstractAgentHostCustomizationService.resolveRuntimePluginEnablement calls listPluginInstallations once per provider, and the connection bridge can cross a remote host. CopilotAgent.listPluginInstallations always invokes global plugins.list and then invokes the live session's plugins.list when available. ItemProviderItemSource caches only the whole provider promise until onDidChange, so a new source or each invalidation repeats the boundary.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache/coalesce inventory by provider, backend session, and exact chat, invalidating after runtime mutations or host activation-change events. Preserve the advertised default-chat value when authoritative, and avoid withholding the entire item list while an exact-chat refresh is in flight.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create/resume a Copilot chat and publish its runtime-owned plugin customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create/resume awaits ActiveClient.snapshot -> getAppliedCustomizations; session-state publication and getChatCustomizations await getCustomizationsSettled. The diff places runtime inventory refresh and cold plugin parsing before these paths can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Global Copilot SDK plugins.list inventory RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per runtime inventory refresh, independent of plugin count; repeats for every settled/applied snapshot and every queued refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Settled/applied customization snapshots did not invoke plugin inventory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Live session Copilot SDK plugins.list inventory RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional call after the global inventory when installed plugins exist and a live session is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No session-effective plugin inventory call existed on these snapshot paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs serially after the global RPC and blocks exact effective enablement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Detect plugin format, read manifest, resolve component directories, and read component files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold cost is once per installed plugin per active SessionPluginController; repeated after version/file/discovery invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Runtime-owned installed plugin content was not parsed or recursively watched by each session controller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold parsing is awaited by _readRuntimePlugins and therefore by create/resume/publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S active configuration scopes, P installed plugins, and R settled/applied snapshot or publication requests; inventory RPC work grows with S×R, while cold parsing/listener state grows with S×P.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin files are parsed in Promise.all within a refresh. Refreshes use a per-session Sequencer, which serializes every request but does not coalesce duplicates; global and live SDK inventory calls are serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parsed content is cached by resource/version only inside each session and invalidated by file/version/refreshDiscovery. Cold sessions independently parse all P plugins; warm sessions reuse parsed content but still perform fresh inventory RPCs. No negative/current inventory cache or in-flight coalescing exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: session-local ownership, parser I/O, unconditional refresh callers, Sequencer behavior, and downstream RPCs are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed-plugin and simultaneously active-session counts vary, and SDK RPC/file latency is environment-dependent, especially for remote filesystems.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: duplicated per-session parse/watch caches and uncoalesced inventory RPCs create concrete S×P retained/I/O cost and repeated critical-path IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh Chat Customizations for a selected host chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideChatSessionCustomizations now awaits resolveRuntimePluginEnablement before it can iterate, expand, or return any customization item, so inventory completion gates initial list rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct runtime provider represented in the snapshot on each uncached item-provider fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider used the published customization snapshot directly with no management call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks all customization item enumeration and rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot global and optional exact-chat plugins.list SDK calls behind the management bridge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For Copilot, one global call and optionally one live-session call per provider inventory request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the customization list did not query runtime plugin inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds serial runtime round trips to the UI fetch; a remote connection can add network transport latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct runtime provider count and item-source recreation/invalidation frequency; calls are grouped per provider rather than per plugin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Providers are queried with Promise.all. Each Copilot provider request performs global then optional live-session inventory serially. Separate item-source invalidations are not coalesced by the resolver.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ItemProviderItemSource caches the whole provider promise until onDidChange, but resolveRuntimePluginEnablement itself has no cache keyed by provider/session/chat; recreated sources and invalidations repeat the calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the blocking await, per-provider call, management bridge, and downstream SDK calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users may have one provider and local IPC, while remote hosts or slow runtimes make the added wait more visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity rendering latency because the diff moves fresh runtime inventory onto the list's blocking path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover globally installed Copilot plugins and toggle global enablement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Discovery reads the installed-plugin state, obtains one runtime inventory, resolves each plugin directory, and publishes discovery. A toggle awaits setPluginEnabled and then an explicit discovery refresh before completing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read installed plugin configuration and resolve each plugin root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration read plus one root resolve per installed plugin per discovery refresh; root resolution was already present before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Installed plugin state and each plugin root were already read/resolved during discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates discovery publication; per-plugin resolve cardinality is pre-existing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped call per discovery refresh, with at most three delayed retries after failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery used local installed state without a runtime inventory call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates publication of runtime-owned plugins; retries occur after the failed discovery rather than as an unbounded burst.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime setPluginEnabled followed by a discovery inventory refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mutation and one refresh for each explicit user toggle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Global enablement used the local model rather than the owning runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks toggle completion until authoritative state is re-read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugin count P, actual config changes, bounded retry attempts, and explicit user toggles.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery refresh versions discard stale results; retry scheduling is bounded to three attempts with exponential delays. Per-plugin root resolves remain sequential as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime inventory is retained in an observable after a successful refresh. Failures clear it and retry at 1/2/4 seconds; retries are canceled/reset on success or empty installation state. Parsed plugin entries are reused by the existing discovery cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary counts and retry behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime inventory latency varies, but refresh triggers and failure retries are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new inventory call is grouped once per discovery, retries are bounded, and mutation refresh is an intentional authoritative read after a user action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and operate inline plugin enablement switches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible plugin rows synchronously create one switch and hover registration when an action exposes checked state; clicking awaits the provider-owned mutation while disabling the switch.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered plugin rows, not total catalog size when the list is virtualized; card rows create one toggle per displayed plugin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each click disables its switch until its single mutation resolves. No loop, subprocess, IPC fan-out, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced directly by rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: DOM nodes and listeners are owned by row/card disposable stores and disposed with the renderer/card surface; no new unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous DOM path and disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large non-virtualized card sections could increase DOM count, but the added node/listener per row is small and no concrete rendering regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue in the toggle renderer itself.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change exact-chat global or repository plugin enablement from a customization action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action validates current exact-chat inventory, then awaits the runtime mutation; repository scope also requires an initialized chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider inventory request per explicit action, expanding to one global and optionally one session SDK list for Copilot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Runtime-owned global/repository mutations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks mutation until readiness and managed state are confirmed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy host/local overlays were used instead of the owning runtime mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action remains disabled until authoritative mutation completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit user actions; cardinality does not scale with plugin collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One switch action disables itself while awaiting completion; no collection-wide concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The validation intentionally reads authoritative current state and does not rely on stale local state. Post-mutation state arrives through runtime/discovery refresh paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary count and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: RPC duration varies, but action frequency is user-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the preflight and mutation are bounded to one explicit action and preserve required readiness/policy semantics.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files. Submitted three findings: session-local runtime plugin parse/watch caches duplicate S×P filesystem and retained state, Sequencer queues uncoalesced inventory RPCs on settled snapshot paths, and customization-list enumeration blocks on uncached runtime inventory. Bounded discovery retries, explicit mutation validation, and inline toggle rendering did not establish additional regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
